dedupe_keys.name: dodgr shortest paths travel times and flow aggregation on dual weighted directed street networks r package

description: dodgr (Distances on Directed Graphs) is an R package on CRAN (version 0.5.0, published 3 September 2026) that computes distances on dual-weighted directed graphs with priority-queue shortest path algorithms (Padgham 2019, doi 10.32866/6945). Contents: weighted directed graphs have weights from A to B that can differ from B to A, and dual-weighted graphs carry two sets of weights; the canonical example is a street network where routes are chosen by weighting distances by way type and transport mode while route lengths are still calculated from direct distances. Vignettes cover the basic workflow, travel times, categorical distances, flows (aggregating or dispersing flows over a network) and parallel computation; the package imports osmdata to build networks from OpenStreetMap. Producer: Mark Padgham (maintainer) with Andreas Petutschnig, David Cooley and contributors including Robin Lovelace. Coverage: any network, typically OpenStreetMap street networks. Format and access: R package with compiled C++ code on CRAN, reference manual and documentation website. Licence: GPL-3 (CRAN metadata). Caveats: it models static network distances and flows, not dynamic traffic assignment with congestion. Simulation uses: accessibility and routing studies for walking, cycling and driving, aggregating origin-destination flows onto links, and testing network disruption by removing edges. Related records: model-stplanr, model-r5r and model-osmnx.
